title: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yitzchak

paragraphs: In [Sukkah 44b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sukkah.44b.6): Aivu said (Rav’s father, [according to Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Sukkah.44b.5.1)): “I was standing before Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yitzchak (according to Dikdukei Soferim’s reading). A man came before him and asked him about a law of the Sabbatical year.” Aivu also [transmits in his name the ruling](https://www.sefaria.org/Sukkah.44b.8) that a person should not walk more than three parasangs on the eve of Shabbat.[^1]
This reading was also before Yuchasin, and Hyman considers [Heilprin’s criticism under Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Tzadok](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=528&lang=en) needless.[^2]

notes.text: The linked Bavli gives Elazar bar Tzadok in both passages. The three-parasang ruling is a prohibition on travel beyond that distance before Shabbat.
Heilprin treats Yuchasin’s Elazar son of Yitzchak as a textual error. Hyman defends that reading and reports it in Dikdukei Soferim.
